gen-comfortaa-gf-copse: Neon-tube strokes define Comfortaa, its spacing stretched like an uncoiled spring and its c a wide ring. But Copse, a serif, settles into literary, classic reading with daylight showing through every curve.
gen-comfortaa-gf-enriqueta: Friendly neon curves, with Comfortaa giving every stroke the same visual weight and stretched spacing. And Enriqueta, the text serif, handles dignified, literary reading, its chalky curves stopping short of closing.
gen-comfortaa-gf-habibi: Bent-wire friendly letters: Comfortaa stretches its spacing like an uncoiled spring, loose and open. And Habibi, a serif, grounds those loops with a traditional, editorial voice and open channels into each round letter.
gen-comfortaa-gf-inika: Inika, a serif with a visible gap in each s, sits beneath a Comfortaa heading drawn with steady pen pressure. Classic, traditional warmth meeting friendly geometry is the whole appeal.
gen-comfortaa-gf-kay-pho-du: Rounded and glowing, Comfortaa stretches its friendly geometric letters out like an uncoiled spring. And Kay Pho Du, the text serif, brings traditional steadiness, its counters breathing like a hollow reed cut open.
gen-comfortaa-gf-labrada: Labrada, a dignified, bookish serif with wide openings on small letters, sits under a friendly, geometric Comfortaa heading. Heading joins match stroke thickness, while the serif below stays scholarly.
gen-comfortaa-gf-podkova: Pipe-cleaner curves, friendly and geometric: Comfortaa stretches its spacing like an uncoiled spring. And Podkova, the text serif, brings a bookish, traditional feel with a c opening broad and welcoming.
gen-dafont-aaargh-fs-bespoke-slab: Aaargh, a strong, commanding display face with bowls and stems at matching weight, leads over Bespoke Slab, a serif. Its tall lowercase adds grounded, refined counterweight beneath the loud heading.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-neco: Neco, a classic serif, swells gently from hairline to stem. Against the tall, tightly jammed letters of Franchise, its open, dignified curves carry the real authority of the pair.
gen-dafont-hero-general-sans: General Sans fills the line with open, smoothly bending letters. Hero is best at slow, closed, widely spaced sweeps in big display type, while General Sans handles the running text.
